text.p: Electro-Catheter Corp son Monday said Nasdaq may delist its stock for failing to meet the market's bid price requirement.
Nasdaq requires that a company's stock trade at over $1.00 per share, or alternatively that its book value exceed $2 million, to remain listed on the SmallCap Market index.
Electro-Catheter closed Monday at 21/32, and the company said its current book value was slightly less than $1 million.

The company, which makes diagnostic and therapeutic catheters and related products, said in a news release that its possible delisting would be subject to an oral hearing, to be scheduled no sooner than the end of August.
Earlier Monday, Electro-Catheter reported a third-quarter loss of $0.03 per share, compared to a loss of $0.05 per share for the same period a year ago.
The company said it was still examining financing options for its operations and was in discussions with several medical-device companies about strategic alliances or investments.

Electro-Catheter also said an agreement in principle with an unnamed company was terminated in May at the request of the other company. Electro-Catheter said it received $600,000 for the work it performed and is scheduled to receive a $100,000 termination fee.
